main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2014
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2014 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth
main.subtitle: Explore Isaac’s rebuilt dungeons and changing item combinations
main.summary: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth is a 2014 roguelike action-adventure game designed by Edmund McMillen and developed and published by Nicalis.

cards.heading: Isaac returns to the basement
cards.text: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth is a 2014 roguelike action adventure designed by Edmund McMillen and developed by Nicalis. Isaac escapes into a basement filled with randomly arranged rooms, fighting monsters with tears and collecting items that alter his abilities. Each combination can change how a run plays. Rebirth rebuilds the 2011 Flash game in a new engine; it first appeared on computers, PlayStation 4 and PlayStation Vita before reaching further platforms.

cards.heading: A new engine and the expansion campaigns
cards.text: Rebirth is a remake of The Binding of Isaac, which was developed by McMillen and Florian Himsl and released in 2011 as an Adobe Flash application. This platform had limitations and led McMillen to work with Nicalis to produce Rebirth with a more advanced game engine, which in turn enabled the substantial addition of content and gameplay features. Since release, Rebirth has had four expansions: Afterbirth (2015), Afterbirth+ (2017), Repentance (2021) and Repentance+ (2024) with more game content and gameplay modes. Afterbirth+ also added support for user-created content.

cards.heading: Tears, randomized dungeons and changing co-op modes
cards.text: Isaac's flight into the basement draws on the biblical story of his name and McMillen's religious upbringing. His mother believes that killing him will fulfil God's wishes. The player guides him through random dungeons, using tears as projectiles while collected items change his appearance, attributes and attacks. Rebirth also introduced a supporting cooperative player, expanded to three additional players in Afterbirth. Repentance later allowed four players to choose full characters for local co-op, and Repentance+ added online co-op in November 2024.

cards.heading: Critical reception and the combined sales milestone
cards.text: Reviewers praised Rebirth's combinations and the improvements made possible by rebuilding the original game, while its graphic imagery remained contentious. The expansions continued to add content and challenge, with difficulty becoming a recurring point in their reception. By July 2015, the original Binding of Isaac and Rebirth had sold more than five million copies between them. That figure covers both releases, reflecting the audience carried from the Flash game into its expanded successor.

main.title: Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare
main.subtitle: Explore Sledgehammer’s future war and the rise of Atlas
main.summary: Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare is a 2014 first-person shooter game published by Activision.

cards.heading: Sledgehammer leads a new Call of Duty project
cards.text: Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare is Activision's 2014 first-person shooter and Sledgehammer Games' first turn as the series' lead developer. Its Exo suits let soldiers boost, dash and jump through a future battlefield. Sledgehammer made the PlayStation 4, Windows and Xbox One versions, while High Moon handled PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. The campaign follows Jack Mitchell's involvement with Atlas, a private military corporation.

cards.heading: Atlas, Exo equipment and Pick 13
cards.text: The campaign takes place between 2054 and 2061, with Troy Baker playing Mitchell and Kevin Spacey portraying Atlas leader Jonathan Irons. Exo equipment supplies both movement and abilities such as temporary cloaking, and completed missions award points for upgrades. Boosts and aerial movement also change multiplayer encounters. Pick 13 gives players a thirteen-point allowance for weapons, attachments, perks and score-streaks, making the loadout another set of choices before the fighting begins.

cards.heading: Reception of the faster-paced sequel
cards.text: Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare was released to a positive critical reception and was declared an improvement over its predecessor, Call of Duty: Ghosts. Many critics praised the visuals, voice acting, single-player campaign, and fast-paced gameplay, but some criticized the single-player campaign's plot as predictable. Retrospective reviews have generally remained positive, with the game generally placing in the top 10 in lists ranking the series' games. The game won several awards and was considered a commercial success.

main.title: Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker
main.subtitle: A tiny world worth turning around
main.summary: Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker is Nintendo's miniature puzzle adventure, first released for Wii U in Japan on 13 November 2014.

cards.heading: A tiny world worth turning around
cards.text: Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker is Nintendo's miniature puzzle adventure, first released for Wii U in Japan on 13 November 2014. Captain Toad and Toadette cross compact diorama-like levels, looking for treasure and rescuing one another from Wingo. Their heavy backpacks keep them from jumping, making the shape of the route especially important. A ledge that looks unreachable from one side may connect to a hidden passage behind it, so rotating the view becomes a practical part of finding the way through each small world.

cards.heading: Solve the route without a jump
cards.text: The Wii U GamePad lets the player turn the camera and interact with the scene. That change of viewpoint reveals paths, enemies and items concealed by the level's own structure. Walking, climbing and plucking objects provide the main tools, while optional collectibles and challenges give another reason to inspect a completed stage. The limited movement makes the environment carry the puzzle: the player studies where a path begins, what blocks it and which viewpoint exposes the connection to the destination.

cards.heading: A side activity becomes a whole adventure
cards.text: The idea grew from Captain Toad's stages in Super Mario 3D World. Directors Kenta Motokura and Shinya Hiratake developed it into a complete game, with music by Naoto Kubo and Mahito Yokota. The backpack supplies a character-based explanation for the restriction that defines the design. Switch and Nintendo 3DS editions followed in 2018 with additional content. The original Wii U release turns a familiar platform world into something to examine from all sides, making careful looking as rewarding as the movement of its small explorer.

main.title: Never Alone
main.subtitle: Follow Nuna and the fox through an Iñupiaq story
main.summary: Never Alone follows an I?upiat girl and an Arctic fox through a puzzle-platform adventure made with Alaska Native storytellers and community members.

cards.heading: Nuna and the fox in an I?upiaq story
cards.text: Never Alone, also known as Kisima Inŋitchuŋa is a puzzle-platform adventure video game developed by Upper One Games and published by E-Line Media and was first released in November 2014. It is based on the traditional Iñupiaq tale, "Kunuuksaayuka", which was first recorded by storyteller Robert Nasruk Cleveland in his collection Stories of the Black River People. Swapping between an Iñupiat girl named Nuna and her Arctic fox companion, the player completes puzzles while part of the story is narrated in the Iñupiaq language. The game was made in partnership between the Cook Inlet Tribal Council and E-Line Media and is a video game produced by Indigenous people. A DLC, titled Never Alone: Foxtales was released on July 28, 2015 and a sequel was announced in February 2022. The game received multiple awards and is praised positively for its concept, story and art design but criticized for its platforming elements.

cards.heading: Working with the community
cards.text: The Cook Inlet Tribal Council and E-Line Media developed the project with community members who contributed stories, voices and guidance on their representation. Elders and storytellers helped shape how I?upiaq traditions appeared in the game.

cards.heading: Two companions with different abilities
cards.text: Nuna handles tools and objects, while the more agile fox can interact with spiritual elements. Puzzles require their abilities in combination. A single player switches between the pair, or two players can control one character each in local cooperation.

cards.heading: The Cultural Insights interviews
cards.text: Unlockable Cultural Insights videos feature community members discussing the traditions, places and practices behind the adventure. These interviews accompany the story and explain connections between its scenes and I?upiaq life.

cards.heading: The development team visits Alaska
cards.text: E-Line Creative Director Sean Vesce was excited by the opportunity to "go into a community, learn more about a culture and then try to infuse their values and mythologies into a game".  Vesce and his team made "a dozen trips to Alaska" to meet with community members and gather stories and imagery and was "blown away at the richness and beauty and depth of that storytelling tradition". He realized that "none of that had really been ever explored in a videogame". Vesce previously held leadership positions at Crystal Dynamics and Activision. Vesce built and led a 12-member development team in Seattle, who worked in deep partnership with "40 Alaska Native elders, storytellers and community members" to craft the game. Never Alone was built in the Unity game engine. A local-cooperative mode is available.

cards.heading: Awards for the debut and its cultural impact
cards.text: Never Alone received many accolades, including the British Academy Games Award for Best Debut Game, as well as Game of the Year and Most Significant Impact awards from the Games for Change organization. In 2014, Never Alone was an Official Selection Finalist at Indiecade. At The Game Awards 2014, Never Alone received a nomination in the "Games for Change" category. In 2015, Never Alone received nominations for Outstanding Achievement in Game Direction from the AIAS' D.I.C.E. Awards, Best Debut from the Game Developers Choice Awards, and Matthew Crump Cultural Innovation Award from the SXSW Gaming Awards.  Never Alone also won an Interactive Narrative and Game + Play Peabody Award in 2021.

cards.heading: Praise for the art and divided views on platforming
cards.text:
Critics positively noted the game's art design, which blends a simple, cartoon style with scrimshaw influences. The included documentary videos were also remarked upon as "[leaving the player] feeling educated as well as entertained" and "[doing] an excellent job of giving a cultural context" for the game. In their review, Wired cited the cultural insights as "the best parts of Never Alone".

The platforming elements of Never Alone were more divisive. Some reviewers described the game as "frustrating", noting imprecise controls and inconsistent behavior by in-game characters. However, other critics felt the gameplay was diverse and "satisfying".

cards.heading: Never Alone enters the Museum of Modern Art
cards.text: In 2022 the Museum of Modern Art included the game in their exhibition Never Alone: Video Games and Other Interactive Design and is now a permanent addition to MOMA's evolving collection of nearly 200,000 pieces of modern and contemporary art.

main.title: Dragon Age: Inquisition
main.subtitle: Lead the Inquisition across Thedas and close the Breach
main.summary: Dragon Age: Inquisition is a 2014 action role-playing video game developed by BioWare and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: The Inquisitor, the Breach and the world of Thedas
cards.text: Dragon Age: Inquisition is a 2014 action role-playing video game developed by BioWare and published by Electronic Arts. The third major game in the Dragon Age franchise, Inquisition is the sequel to Dragon Age II (2011). The story follows a player character known as the Inquisitor on a journey to settle the civil unrest in the continent of Thedas and close a mysterious tear in the sky called the "Breach", which is unleashing dangerous demons upon the world. Dragon Age: Inquisition's gameplay is similar to its predecessors, although it consists of several semi-open worlds for players to explore. Players control the Inquisitor or their companions mainly from a third-person perspective, although a traditional role-playing game top-down camera angle is also available.

cards.heading: Responding to feedback while building with Frostbite
cards.text: The release of Dragon Age II was met with a mixed reception from players who lamented the loss of the complexity of the first game, Dragon Age: Origins (2009). BioWare sought to address player feedback for Dragon Age II as a major goal, which influenced the design decisions of its sequel. Ultimately, BioWare wanted the third Dragon Age game to combine the elements of the first two games in the series. Having begun development in 2011, BioWare used EA DICE's Frostbite 3 engine to power the game, though this created many development challenges for the team. They had to crunch extensively during development, and because of hardware limitations on older generation consoles, several gameplay features had to be cut. Trevor Morris composed the game's soundtrack, replacing Inon Zur, the composer used for the previous games.

cards.heading: The original launch, acclaim and later expansions
cards.text: Officially announced in September 2012 as Dragon Age III: Inquisition, the game was released worldwide in November 2014 for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox 360, and Xbox One. Upon release, the game received positive reviews from critics, who praised it for its exploration, combat, writing, characters, and customization. The game received some criticism for its filler content, technical issues, tactical view, and aspects of its narrative. Commercially, it was one of the most successful games released by BioWare. It was awarded numerous accolades and nominated for more, including Game of the Year by several gaming publications. Several narrative downloadable content (DLC) packs were released to support Inquisition. A sequel, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, was released on October 31, 2024.

main.title: Far Cry 4
main.subtitle: Ajay Ghale enters Kyrat’s civil war in Ubisoft’s Himalayan open world
main.summary: Far Cry 4 is a 2014 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: Ajay Ghale, Pagan Min and the Golden Path
cards.text: Far Cry 4 is a 2014 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the successor to the 2012 video game Far Cry 3, and the fourth main installment in the Far Cry series. Set in the fictional Himalayan country of Kyrat, the game follows Ajay Ghale, a young Kyrati-American, who becomes caught in a civil war between Kyrat's Royal Army, controlled by the tyrannical king Pagan Min, and a rebel movement called the Golden Path. The gameplay focuses on combat and open world exploration; players battle enemy soldiers and dangerous wildlife using a wide array of weapons. The game features many elements found in role-playing games, such as a branching storyline and side quests. The game also features a map editor and both cooperative and competitive multiplayer modes.

cards.heading: A new setting shaped by Nepal and cinema
cards.text: Announced in May 2014, development on Far Cry 4 began immediately after the shipment of Assassin's Creed III in late 2012. The team originally intended to develop a direct sequel to Far Cry 3 that continues the narrative, but the idea was later scrapped and the team decided to develop a new setting and story for the game. Certain aspects of Far Cry 4 were inspired by the Nepalese Civil War, and the design of the game's antagonist Pagan Min was inspired by Japanese films Ichi the Killer and Brother. Troy Baker was hired to portray Pagan Min. The game's competitive multiplayer was created by Red Storm Entertainment while the Shangri-La segments in the campaign were handled by Ubisoft Toronto.

cards.heading: Release, critical reception and later games
cards.text: Far Cry 4 was released worldwide for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox 360, and Xbox One in November 2014. It received mostly positive reviews, with critics praising the open-world design, visuals, soundtrack, and characters as well as new gameplay additions and the wealth of content. However, some reviewers disliked the story and found the game too similar to its predecessor. The game sold over 10 million units by March 2020. Several releases of downloadable content were subsequently published. A spin-off title, Far Cry Primal, was released in February 2016. A successor, Far Cry 5, was released in March 2018.

main.title: Tales from the Borderlands
main.subtitle: Rhys and Fiona pursue a Vault through a comic, choice-driven adventure
main.summary: Telltale's episodic adventure follows Rhys and Fiona on a search for a Vault after Borderlands 2.

cards.heading: Telltale brings Borderlands to an episodic adventure
cards.text: Tales from the Borderlands is Telltale Games' episodic adventure in the world created by Gearbox Software. Beginning in November 2014 on computers and home consoles, it follows Hyperion employee Rhys and con artist Fiona on a hunt for a Vault. Dialogue choices and actions carry consequences into later episodes, using the approach Telltale had developed in The Walking Dead and The Wolf Among Us.

cards.heading: Rhys, Fiona and the consequences of player choices
cards.text: Rhys and Fiona's search takes place after Borderlands 2, bringing together two people with different lives and motives. Their alliance gives the adventure its comic exchanges, while choices made along the way affect later parts of the story. Reviewers particularly praised the characters, humour and emotional turns. Some criticised the ageing engine and the familiar structure of Telltale's interactions, but the writing and set pieces gave the journey a strong identity within that format.

cards.heading: The studio’s closure and the game’s return
cards.text: Tales, like many of the other Telltale games, were pulled from sale following the studio's sudden closure in 2018. 2K Games was able to acquire the property and republished the series starting in February 2021. A successor, New Tales from the Borderlands, was released in October 2022.

main.title: Phantasy Star Nova
main.subtitle: A new Phantasy Star expedition is built for Vita
main.summary: Phantasy Star Nova is tri-Ace's PlayStation Vita action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 27 November 2014. It places a customisable character inside a mission-driven adventure with a strong single-player story and encounters against enormous creatures. Completing assignments advances the narrative and expands the possibilities for the developing party. The game shares elements with Phantasy Star Online 2 while changing familiar powers through its own story circumstances. Motoi Sakuraba's score accompanies a portable entry that brings tri-Ace's action role-playing experience into Sega's established science-fiction universe.

cards.heading: A new Phantasy Star expedition is built for Vita
cards.text: Phantasy Star Nova is tri-Ace's PlayStation Vita action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 27 November 2014. It places a customisable character inside a mission-driven adventure with a strong single-player story and encounters against enormous creatures. Completing assignments advances the narrative and expands the possibilities for the developing party. The game shares elements with Phantasy Star Online 2 while changing familiar powers through its own story circumstances. Motoi Sakuraba's score accompanies a portable entry that brings tri-Ace's action role-playing experience into Sega's established science-fiction universe.

cards.heading: Create the weak point before exploiting it
cards.text: Different classes offer close combat, ranged weapons or techniques, while the new Pile weapon fires anchors that can create weak points on enemies. That gives the player a way to change the target rather than merely select an existing vulnerable spot. Weapons are crafted from gathered materials instead of obtained as direct item drops, connecting exploration and combat to preparation. The choice of class determines which tools can be used effectively. A successful mission therefore contributes both to immediate story progress and to the equipment that will make a later giant opponent more manageable.

cards.heading: A personal adventure can become a local expedition
cards.text: The character's name and appearance can be customised using a creation system related to Phantasy Star Online 2. Local ad-hoc cooperation lets up to four Vita players participate together, even as the main story remains central to the design. Sega announced the project in 2013, and a Chinese-language Asian edition followed in 2015. Nova gives the portable series a distinct production identity through tri-Ace and Sakuraba. Its most characteristic encounters connect scale and preparation, asking a comparatively small character to create a useful opening in a creature that occupies much of the battlefield.
